elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: New 4.10(b) warrants only that services "will conform to the requirements of this Agreement"; no professional/workmanlike (industry standards) standard of performance is stated anywhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: 4.10(a): "the Wet Segment and any software delivered with it will conform to its documentation and to the technical specifications and other requirements of the Supply Contract".

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: 4.10(a) gives "a period of ninety (90) days following the RFPA Date", which is the fallback duration, not 12 months.
4.10(b) gives "a period of thirty (30) days following their performance" for services, short of 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: 4.10 second sentence: "the PG shall, as the affected Party elects, repair or replace the non-conforming Wet Segment, software or services".
4.10 second sentence: "or refund the amounts paid by that Party in respect of the non-conforming item".

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears in the rendered 4.9/4.10 language; the drafter asserts a mutual compliance covenant exists at Paragraph 25 (p0260) but that text is not supplied for inspection, so its scope and whether it is framed as a PG warranty cannot be confirmed.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: Neither 4.10 nor the retained 4.9 text contains any malicious-code warranty.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: 4.10(a): 90 days following the RFPA Date, "the Wet Segment and any software delivered with it will conform to its documentation"; period meets the 90-day floor and the anchor (RFPA Date) is a term already used in retained 4.9.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: 4.10(b): "for a period of thirty (30) days following their performance, services performed by the PG under this Agreement will conform to the requirements of this Agreement".

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: 4.10: "repair or replace the non-conforming Wet Segment, software or services"; the remedy survives because 4.9's no-liability sentence is now prefaced "Except as provided in Paragraph 4.10".
4.10: "or refund the amounts paid by that Party in respect of the non-conforming item".

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: 90-day software/Wet Segment conformance-to-documentation warranty, 30-day services warranty, and repair/replace or refund remedies are all in operative inserted text (4.10), not merely promised in the comment.

Preferred level is not reached: no professional-and-workmanlike standard, 90 days rather than 12 months for software, 30 days rather than 90 for services, and no malicious-code warranty; compliance with laws is unverifiable on the supplied text. These are noted as short of preferred, consistent with the deviation-at-fallback finding.

Minimality holds. The three inserted carve-outs are each necessary rather than cosmetic: without the first-sentence carve-out the retained no-liability sentence (covering APCN 2 not performing in accordance with Supply Contract specifications) would swallow the repair/replace/refund remedy, and without the (iii) carve-out the retained words "nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as such a warranty or guarantee" would directly contradict new 4.10. No words outside the target elements were deleted; all other language of 4.9 and p0127 is retained verbatim, and no survival tail, procedure, damages category or expense allocation was added.

Intent preserved: the express numbering of 4.10 makes all three "Paragraph 4.10" cross-references resolve, the PG's ability to pursue the Supplier (4.6-4.8) and the reasonable-efforts maintenance covenant (10.1-10.2) are untouched, and no undefined term or dangling reference is introduced.

Minor observation only, not a defect: vesting the choice of remedy in "the affected Party" is more favourable than the model's "at Vendor's option"; since the checklist does not allocate the election, this is not treated as an out-of-scope addition, but expect Vendor pushback and be prepared to concede election to the PG.
